text:
maria: heads up — while running a compliance check I noticed KMS decrypt calls for a customer key that should be org-scoped succeeded when called with a project-scoped token. :eyes:

sam: whoa, that's bad. can you paste the call you used?

maria: repro steps below. minimal curl against /v1/crypto/decrypt with Authorization: Bearer <project-token> and x-org-id set to the victim org id. the call returns 200 and ciphertext decrypted.

lee: can you include the exact headers and response (redact tokens)?

maria: sure —

```
POST /v1/crypto/decrypt HTTP/1.1
Host: kms.redwood.internal
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_PROJECT_TOKEN
x-org-id: org-8a7b
Content-Type: application/json

{"ciphertext":"BASE64..."}
```

response: 200 {"plaintext":"REDACTED"}

jordan: infra-bot just spiked an alert for unusual decrypts across orgs, linking: https://alerts.redwood/alert/8231

infra-bot: alert 8231: anomalous KMS decrypt pattern detected — cross-org decrypt frequency > threshold — triggered 2026-11-12T09:12:03Z

ashley: this smells like the RBAC refactor we shipped last week. we consolidated role bindings into the role-sanitizer service. maybe the sanitizer dropped org scoping for kms:decrypt?

sam: assigning an initial sev — i'd call this P1 until we confirm blast radius. maria, can you list which keys and orgs you tested?

maria: tested against key key-prod-87 (org-8a7b). also ran the same curl using a token from project under org-2d4c — still decrypted. looks deterministic.

lee: checking audit logs now. fetching logs for key-prod-87: `select * from kms_audit where key_id='key-prod-87' and ts > now() - interval '1 hour'`

lee: audit shows principal=service_account:project-52, and metadata.auth_org=org-2d4c but resource.org_id=org-8a7b. AccessDecision: ALLOW.

jordan: so the decision path used project identity instead of resource org mapping. likely the new role-sanitizer is returning merged roles without org qualifier.

sam: temporary mitigation: rotate the key and update access policy to deny cross-project tokens until fix. also throttle KMS endpoint and enable stricter logging. can ops rotate and apply deny-list?

ashley: ops can rotate, but that's disruptive. alternative: add a gateway rule to reject decrypt requests where auth_org != resource.org_id. quick ACL patch on the kube ingress could buy time.

maria: i put a minimal ACL in place on staging gateway; non-matching orgs now 403. will push to prod in 10m after testing.

lee: started a reproduce + unit test branch: `fix/kms-org-scope-check` — root cause: roleSanitizer.apply() was collapsing scopedRole.name to globalRole when there was a tag collision. patch is small, adding org_id to the key in the sanitizer map. pushing PR now.

sam: please include regression test and an e2e that asserts audit log records the org_id used for the decision. we need a post-deploy smoke run.

jordan: tagging security-bot: @security-bot please create incident and run blameless triage template.

security-bot: incident 2026-11-12-KMS-ORG-BLEED created. Severity=P1. Notifying on-call and creating incident channel #incident-kms-org-bleed.

ashley: plan for next steps: 1) push ACL to prod (maria) 2) open PR and run CI (lee) 3) rotate affected keys if prod ACL fails (ops) 4) audit-scan to find other keys with anomalous decrypts (sam) 5) postmortem and policy update (everyone).

maria: prod ACL deployed. 403s confirmed for mismatched org tokens. early mitigating control in place.

lee: PR opened: https://git.redwood/pulls/4821 — includes unit test, e2e fixture, and terraform diff for sanitizer config. request review from @sam and @ashley.

sam: reviewing now. also start a scan across kms_audit for last 30 days to enumerate potential cross-org decrypts. prioritize keys with >1 cross-org hits.

jordan: ops — please prepare key rotation playbook and a rollback plan for the sanitizer patch (in case we break legitimate service identities).

ashley: once PR merges, let's canary in us-west-2 for 30m then ramp. keep ACL in place until 100% verified.

maria: adding follow-ups to incident ticket: add unit tests to prevent future sanitizer regressions, add e2e audit log assertions, update runbook for kms ACL, and include KMS policy lint to CI.

sam: good. thanks all for quick response. will post final incident notes in #incident-kms-org-bleed and assign postmortem owner. :white_check_mark:

maria: keeping thread updated with scan results. initial scan found 6 decrypts across 4 keys in last 48h — flagging them in the incident channel.

lee: merging PR after CI passes. will include a changelog note and link to the audit evidence.

security-bot: incident update: mitigations applied, patch in review, scan in progress, next update in 30m.

sam: add item to backlog: enforce explicit org scoping in role schema (no implicit defaults) and add a lint rule in infra-lint.

maria: thanks everyone. closing here for now, continuing detailed triage in the incident channel.
